\begin{frame}{Why JARVIS is not just a chatbot}
\subt{\chg{A chatbot answers questions. JARVIS lives inside Tony Stark's workspace: it knows his projects, uses his machines and asks before acting.\\
\medskip
Four features make the difference.}}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Memory}{Remembers projects, past choices, constraints and an evolving work history.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Tools}{Reads files and interacts with authorized applications and systems.}
\end{columns}\vspace{1mm}
\begin{columns}[c,onlytextwidth]\column{.485\textwidth}
\sboxblue{Context}{Knows which project, artifact and stage of work matters now.}
\column{.485\textwidth}
\coursebox{Action}{Executes constrained workflows, reports progress and asks for approval.}
\end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Chatbot → agent → agent with a Brain}
\subt{A Second Brain \chg{is an infrastructure} outside the harness.}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{.6em}
\item \textbf{Chatbot.} \chg{Answers only from what is in the current conversation: your messages and the files you paste in.}
\item \textbf{Agent.} Can plan tool calls, read files and change the environment within permissions.
\item \textbf{Persistent Brain.} Adds durable project state, approved decisions, sources, skills and working procedures.
\item \textbf{Control loop.} Human review, version history and a closeout protocol prevent invisible drift.
\end{itemize}
\takeaway{Assistant quality = model capability + relevant memory + tools + controls.}
\end{frame}
